clue.text: Reveal body, one torn angrily

definitions.meaning: to undress completely, baring the body
a strip that comes off, as in the British idiom of tearing a ... someone, meaning to scold them furiously

explanation.surface: Someone angrily ripping their clothes away to bare themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'tear a strip off' someone is British slang for a furious telling-off, so the thing torn angrily is a strip, off.
explanation.definitionFit: Peeling away every garment exposes the body, which is what undressing fully does.

clue.text: Thump one with wind

definitions.meaning: the windsock at an airfield, which fills with the breeze

explanation.surface: Hitting someone who is breathless or gassy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sock is slang for a hard punch, and a windsock is a sock that catches wind.

clue.text: First off, took water level

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: drank, as in swallowed water

explanation.surface: Someone who drank water first, then got level.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means a level or grade in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Perhaps it's clear she's a nun

parts.note: read as wordplay, the name Clare with poor as an anagram signal would make the word clear

explanation.surface: Remarking that it is obvious a woman has taken holy orders.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as an anagram instruction (poorly arranged CLARE), produces 'clear'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poor Clares are an order of Franciscan nuns founded by St Clare.

clue.text: Settle in, as one might do in I dns?

definitions.text: Settle in, as one might do in I dns?

parts.words: Settle in, as one might do in I dns?
parts.note: the italic letters look like a phrase with pieces missing, leaving only some word endings, so whoever reads it is locating the feet

explanation.surface: Advice on adapting to a new place, with a puzzling fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to adjust and grow confident; the italic jumble is a playful picture of word-ends or feet being sought.
explanation.definitionFit: To find one's feet is to become settled and confident in new surroundings.

clue.text: Castle is at far end of county

indicators.note: the word is is placed after the county, at its far end

parts.note: Glam is the short form of Glamorgan, a Welsh county

explanation.surface: Directions saying a castle stands at the remote edge of a county.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan was a county in south Wales; its abbreviation is GLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamis Castle in Angus, Scotland, is famous from Macbeth and as the Queen Mother's childhood home.

clue.text: Boys accept love in quantity

parts.note: lads are boys
love is zero in tennis, hence O

explanation.surface: Young men accepting affection in abundance.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads, informally, means a great deal or in large amounts.

clue.text: Grand catamaran redesigned — monarch had to accept it

indicators.note: the boat's letters are reshaped into a new form

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A big yacht is remodelled, and a king must put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: King John was compelled to seal the charter at Runnymede in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Charter was forced upon King John by his barons, so a monarch had to accept it.

clue.text: Discord, being taken off the job

definitions.meaning: in music, a note held over into a chord where it clashes
temporary removal from work, often pending an inquiry

explanation.surface: Workplace strife leading to someone being sent home.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspension is both a musical dissonance and a temporary barring from work.

clue.text: Mix up, but prisoner recaptured

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict
found, as when an escaped man is located and taken again

explanation.surface: Confusion reigns after an escaped convict is caught once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound is to confuse, muddling one thing with another.

clue.text: Witch is eating good national dish

indicators.note: the witch-and-is pair takes the letter for good inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: a hag is an ugly old witch

explanation.surface: A witch tucking into a fine plate of her country's signature food.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is regarded as Scotland's national dish, a savoury pudding of offal and oats.

clue.text: Pop idol?

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad
a figure is a statue or image, like an idol

explanation.surface: Asking about a chart-topping singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop idol suggests a pop star, but the whole clue describes a man looked up to as a dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A father figure is an older man revered as a parent, a dad who is idolised.

clue.text: She married Don for a quick win

definitions.meaning: a woman who wed a university don, a scholar, would be that scholar's wife
a four-move checkmate in chess, the fastest common way to beat a novice

explanation.surface: A woman who wed an academic, apparently in record time.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, so his wife is a scholar's mate; in chess the same phrase names a four-move checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the classic quick checkmate on f7, and literally also means a scholar's spouse.

clue.text: Is parted from husband underground? Almost a disaster

annotationWithheld.why: Is parted from husband underground? Almost a disaster (5,5): the parse is LOSES H inside CAVE, but 'underground' must give CAVE and also signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Is parted from husband underground? Almost a disaster

clue.text: Playing well, partner, in relaxed fashion

parts.note: a player in form is performing well
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: Two partners playing well together in a casual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally means in a casual, relaxed manner without ceremony.

clue.text: Notice nothing about girl

indicators.note: the whole run of notice then nothing is turned round

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone noticing nothing whatever about a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a girl's name, the usual crossword sense of girl.

clue.text: Sine shape is wavy you find this in a good book

definitions.text: you find this in a good book

indicators.note: a wavy line is distorted, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark on the undulating form of a sine curve, then a pious aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The good book is the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesians is a New Testament epistle, a book within the Bible.

clue.text: Two fools go for woodpecker

parts.note: a sap is a fool
a sucker is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A pair of idiots pick a woodpecker.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapsuckers are North American woodpeckers that drill trees to drink sap.

clue.text: Claimed to know, following inside track

indicators.note: the knowing and following letters go within the track

parts.note: spoor is the track or trail of an animal
ken means to know, in Scottish usage
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Someone asserting knowledge while tracking from within.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken for is already reserved or claimed by another.

clue.text: Courtyard is in occupation

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the word occupation

explanation.surface: A remark that a courtyard is currently being used.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved courtyard or open area next to a house.

clue.text: Sort of stone house, much loved

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house in British usage
precious means dearly loved

explanation.surface: A stone-built house that its owners adore.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is a British house joined to one neighbour by a shared wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Semiprecious describes gems such as amethyst valued below diamonds and rubies.

clue.text: One calling about break-up

indicators.note: in a down entry the about-and-break pair is read upwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a gap is a break

explanation.surface: Someone phoning about the end of a relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager is a device that calls or beeps its holder, so something that calls.

clue.text: Game up as pompous courtier is half exposed

indicators.note: only half of the courtier's name is shown

parts.note: Polonius is the self-important courtier in Hamlet

explanation.surface: A match is over now that a stuffy courtier is half naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' marks the top half of the name in this down entry, the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a game played on horseback with mallets.

clue.text: While speaking, plugs in tool for carpenter

indicators.note: signals the word for plugs is said aloud

parts.note: ads are advertisements, plugs

explanation.surface: A carpenter talks while fitting plugs into wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is a cutting tool with an arched blade used to shape timber.

clue.text: Maintain a shelf soundly

indicators.note: signals the letters are what a shelf sounds like when spoken

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Insisting that a shelf is sturdy.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or maintain that something is so.

clue.text: Spy on boat? Security not costly

indicators.note: the spy comes after the boat, set on it

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing boat
James Bond is fiction's best-known spy

explanation.surface: An agent aboard a vessel, and a comment on cheap safety.
explanation.walkthrough: The spy is placed after the boat, as if standing on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A junk bond is a high-yield, low-rated security, so cheaply priced.

clue.text: Donkey engine lost its insides long ago

indicators.note: only the first and last letters of engine remain once its middle is gone

parts.note: yore means time long past

explanation.surface: A donkey-engine that was gutted long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: A donkey engine is a small auxiliary engine, which makes 'Donkey engine' look like one thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eeyore is the gloomy donkey in A. A. Milne's Winnie-the-Pooh stories.

clue.text: Female, to listener, a bit terrifying

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens
some means a certain amount, a bit

explanation.surface: A woman who seems, to whoever hears her, slightly frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearsome means frightening, causing fear.
